en.title: Marvel's Original Human Torch Could Ignite a WWII Storyline
en.summary: The creator behind the new Vision series wants to bring back a foundational Marvel character for a World War II adventure. This move could deepen the MCU's connection to its earliest comic book roots.
en.body:
The creator of the recent Disney+ series *VisionQuest* has expressed a desire to see Marvel's very first superhero, the original **Human Torch**, make a significant return in a World War II setting. This sentiment, shared by **Paul Bettany** (who plays Vision), could pave the way for a fascinating exploration of the character's untapped potential within the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

In *VisionQuest* Episode 7, the android **Vision** encountered **J.I.M.**, an artificial intelligence that serves as a direct nod to **Jim Hammond**, the original Human Torch. Created by scientist **Phineas Horton**, Hammond first appeared in *Marvel Comics #1* in 1939, predating even **Captain America**. He was Marvel's first true superhero, an android capable of spontaneous combustion, who eventually learned to control his fiery abilities. While the moniker was later famously adopted by **Johnny Storm** of the **Fantastic Four**, the original android's legacy is now officially canonized within the MCU, tied directly to Vision's own complex origin story.

The appeal of a World War II narrative featuring the original **Human Torch** is significant. In the comics, Hammond fought alongside **Captain America** and **Namor** during that era, making him a key figure in Marvel's early superhero history. Bringing this aspect to the screen would not only honor the character's comic book origins but also provide a fresh perspective on the war-time adventures that laid the groundwork for many of Marvel's iconic heroes. The possibility of seeing this fiery android clash with Nazi forces offers a dramatic and historically resonant storyline that could appeal to both long-time comic fans and newcomers to the Marvel universe.

## A Fiery Legacy Rekindled

The introduction of **J.I.M.** in *VisionQuest* has already sparked considerable excitement among fans, especially those who appreciate Marvel's deep comic book lore. This character's presence in the MCU, directly linked to Vision's creation and Marvel's earliest days, suggests a broader intention to integrate more of the publisher's foundational elements. The idea of **Jim Hammond** going head-to-head with Nazis is a powerful visual and narrative concept that resonates with the heroic ideals of the Golden Age. It’s a chance to not only revisit a pivotal period in fictional history but also to showcase a hero whose origins are intrinsically tied to technological advancement and the dawn of the superhero era.

## What's Next for the Torch?

While specific plans for a World War II story featuring the original **Human Torch** have not yet been officially announced by Marvel Studios, the creative team's expressed interest is a promising sign. The successful integration of **J.I.M.** into *VisionQuest* has proven the character's viability within the current MCU framework. Fans will be eagerly watching for any further developments, hoping that this classic hero will indeed get his chance to shine on the global stage, perhaps in a future project or series that delves deeper into Marvel's rich past.

However, the episode’s most notable moment came when Vision confronts J.I.M., one of the Marvel universe’s earliest examples of artificial intelligence and, in some ways, the original Human Torch. There’s quite a lot of Marvel history to break down involving this, but here’s the gist. In Marvel Comics, the scientist Phineas Horton created what would later be referred to as one of Marvel’s first synthetic humans, Jim Hammond. Though quite advanced for his time, Hammond suffered from a nasty case of spontaneous combustion that he was later able to control, effectively becoming Marvel’s first Human Torch in the process. In fact, this Human Torch was the cover star of Marvel Comics #1 in 1939, making him one of Marvel’s first superheroes. The moniker was later reused for Johnny Storm of the Fantastic Four, but the original Human Torch certainly has his place in Marvel history. The VisionQuest version of that character (known as J.I.M.) is a bit different from the comic book version of the character. Most notably, he looks like Paul Bettany, bursts into flames when he gets emotional, and has a more modern, AI-friendly moniker. But he is essentially the MCU’s take on that character. Although, technically, we previously saw an apparent version of Jim Hammond encased in glass in the Stark Expo scene in Captain America: The First Avenger , but… well, who has time for all of that? The upshot is that the MCU has officially introduced a fully realized version of that character. And to hear showrunner Terry Matalas tell it, he’d love to do more with that character in the future. “That should be a show… When he gets emotional, he overloads. It’s such a great metaphor,” Matalas tells Entertainment Weekly . “I’ve got some crazy ideas about how to tell that story, but, yeah, you would love to see him run around in World War II and be a part of things… I wanna see that guy go up against the Nazis.” At the moment, that seems like more of a wish from Mata
